about.author: Author

tour.hint: Click anywhere to continue · Esc to exit

welcome.title: Welcome to Merger Lab
welcome.body: This quick guide walks through the app's main parts. Click anywhere to move on (Esc to exit at any time).

loadFiles.title: 1. Load your files
loadFiles.body: Add the .xlsx, .xls, .csv or .ods files you want to combine. The order in the list matters: you can reorder them by dragging.

csvFiles.title: 2. CSV files
csvFiles.body: When you load a .csv, the app detects its separator on its own (comma, semicolon, tab…). You can change it manually and preview the first rows; if the detection is not sure, you will see a warning like this one.

chooseMode.title: 3. Choose how to combine them
chooseMode.body: Join matches files by a key column; Stack joins them one below the other when they share the same columns. Each mode has its own tutorial with diagrams (the "?" button).

joinType.title: 4. Join type
joinType.body: In join mode you choose how the files are matched: Inner, Left, Right or Outer. If you are not sure which one to use, the "?" button explains each type with drawings and examples.

joinKey.title: 5. Key column per file
joinKey.body: In join mode you choose which column identifies each row in EACH file separately — they can have different names, the app treats them as the same key when combining.

configureOutput.title: 6. Configure the output
configureOutput.body: Choose the resulting file's format, its name and the folder where it will be saved.

merge.title: 7. Combine
merge.body: Once the button is enabled, combine the files. If it's disabled, the text above will tell you exactly what's missing.

theme.title: 8. Light or dark theme
theme.body: By default it follows the operating system's theme; choose "Light" or "Dark" to set it manually.

help.title: 9. Help and version
help.body: Here you'll find the version, the author, and a link to watch this tour again whenever you want.

joinTutorial.title: Join types
joinTutorial.chainNote: If you combine more than two files, the join is applied in a chain, in the order they appear in the list: first file 1 with file 2, then that result with file 3, and so on.

inner.title: Inner join (intersection)
inner.description: Only rows whose key column exists in ALL combined files are kept. Example: who has both health insurance AND a gym membership.

left.title: Left join
left.description: All rows from the first file are kept, filled in with data from the others when the key matches (blank if there's no match). Example: everyone with health insurance, whether or not they have a gym membership.

right.title: Right join
right.description: The mirror of a left join: all rows from the other file are kept, filled in with data from the first when it matches. Example: everyone with a gym membership, whether or not they have health insurance.

outer.title: Outer join (full)
outer.description: All rows from every file are kept, whether they match or not. Missing data is left blank. Example: everyone with health insurance OR a gym membership (or both).

stackTutorial.title: How stacking rows works
stackTutorial.body1: Stacking takes each file and places its rows one below the other, in the order they appear in the list. It doesn't cross data between files: it just concatenates them. Columns are aligned by name; if a file is missing a column the others have, that cell is left blank in its rows.
stackTutorial.body2: Use this mode when the files represent the same kind of data repeated over time or in batches (for example, sales for January, February and March with the same columns), unlike a join, which crosses different columns using a shared key.
stackTutorial.sourceColumnTerm: Add a column with the source file name
stackTutorial.sourceColumnNote: adds an extra column indicating which file each row came from, useful for tracing its origin after stacking.
